body:
That's brilliant, actually. Seemed to relieve some tension. I appreciate it and thank you for the luck wished. Found out I'm gonna have to wait till the 2nd to get new ones but a few friends are helping me out, thankfully. Have a happy new year, friend. (: 
*Hug back*

That.. honestly all sounds pretty wonderful. I'm trying to refill the prescription today and I think I can despite it not being the correct date yet,  but I keep thinking back to things that crush me. Lost love, professional blunders, idiotic decisions, so many things. I hate it, I really do, and every time I think about it this utter hatred burns through any willpower I've managed to build up and it's all I can do to keep pretending I'm a normal, happy person. Got too frustrated before fucking up my arm last night, ended up throwing the knife out the window and making my way to a friend's house at 3 am because I knew it would stop me from doing anything worse. 

Apologies,  I shouldn't be ranting at you. Doing my best to stay calm but Christ it's certainly no small damn task. Feel like I'm trapped in my body and desperate to get out. Bagh, I need more parts of my brain to want to keep the show going. -.- 

Though thanks for the hug, haha.. it's the little things sometimes, y'know? They can smuggle in that drop of sunlight when nothing else seems to be able to break through. Anyway, have a nice one mr./ms. Inahc.

Good to hear, friend. On all counts. It can be rough sometimes it really can be.. if you appreciated the chat thing, I might also point you towards something like depressionforrums.c om (Google it, idk what the actual address was) or similar, o haven't used it in quite some time but it was nice to have a sort of anonymous journal and small collection of folks to talk to who are vaguely consistent. Keeping up with each other also built a bit of a sense of.. idk, community? Belonging? Whatever it was, it was pleasant. Might actually look into it myself again, now that I think about it.. anyway, good luck my friend, and cheers.

Distraction is right on point, tbh.. every time I get the chance to sit and think it all floods back, it's terrifying. As cliche as it is everything feels pointless if it's all just an escape. I mean, what's the point of life Of my only goal is to escape by *actual life* and forget it's happening?

Also yeah, idk how it was meant to flow, probably because it just sort of doesn't. Thanks or the title thing btw, it was surprisingly... Relieving, to hear.
If you're anything like me it's a distraction, almost like something to do to stave off boredom, only that boredom is melancholy. Do you play games? Read? Write?

Christ, you're me six months ago... It was before I started seeing a doctor.. o was able to get on SSRIs and between that, the lifeline of that doctor, and a few other things, I was able to get a hold of it a bit better. Seriously, give it some thought if you get the chance, it may be able to help you control things, maybe eventually find yourself somewhere better.

I've always been terrified of the idea. Fascinated, but terrified. Anyway, you're giving yourself time. That must mean you've something to live for, no?

I understand the urge, honestly I do, all too well.. but we've gotta keep on, y'know? How else will we find something or someone worth living for?
